page: Microsoft Azure F32als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Falsv6 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a single thread per core configuration, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware allocation includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It lacks local storage and integrated GPUs, but supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and single-core computational capabilities. The server achieved a top-tier rating in Geekbench multi-core testing and small-model LLM prompt processing. It also demonstrated strong performance in stress-ng CPU tests, Passmark CPU metrics, and Redis SET operations. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and static web serving throughput remain in the average tier, reflecting the constraints of the 2.0 GB per core memory allocation.

The F32als_v6 offers high compute density relative to its memory footprint, making it a cost-efficient option for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory arrays or local storage. Tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and a low memory-to-vCPU ratio, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, ray tracing, and small-to-medium scale LLM inference.
